label: digit 3 input in first three original positions
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the digit 3 during the original phase, almost entirely at positions t=0..2 (every such step fires). Magnitude falls with position: near max (~2.35) at t=0, somewhat lower at t=1, about half at t=2 (activation-mass share 0.44/0.38/0.18 on similar counts). At t=3 it fires weakly on a minority of 3s, and almost never later. It does not fire on any other token, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase, including when 3 is fed back as an output (about 119 tiny exceptions). A repeated 3 early in the sequence still fires, at reduced strength.

issues: This run only checked the feature claim. It did not estimate batch 2 timing or launch batch 3, which was the relayed user request.

I found no systematic counterexample class. On the test split the predicate has precision 1.0, with 0 false positives, so every original-phase 3 at t<=2 fires. Recall is 0.956 and mass recall is 0.996.

All 2290 test misses are weak activations at t=3 (about 0.02 to 0.16 of max) on original-phase 3s. They hold only 0.4% of activation mass. None of the subsets I tried separates them: only 14% of t=3 3s fire, whether or not a 3 appeared earlier, and none fire at L=3. They look like a graded tail falling off with position, not a missing condition.

The profile matches the explanation. 119 copy-phase activations are negligible, there are 0 activations on <DEL>, and only token 3 is active. Mass shares by t are 0.435 / 0.378 / 0.183 / 0.004, with max 2.349.
Minor point: with t<=2 the label's 'first three original positions' wording is exact. Hedging it as 'early' would also be fine.
